new_statements.quote: The wordlist was collected as a 'one-shot' exercise and the transcription must therefore be regarded as very preliminary. In general, tones are not marked, although the data was taped and they will be added when time permits. [...] Doubled vowels are common, but frequent tonal changes suggests these should always be analysed as VV sequences, arising from vowel assimilation and intervocalic consonant loss. [...] 3.3 Tones. Tone on verb stems tends to be predictable as with many Kambari lects.
new_statements.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2006. The Lopa language of Northwestern Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment (printout 2 June 2006). Cambridge: Mallam Dendo. 27 pp. [Glottolog ref 16298, listed by Glottolog as a wordlist, filed under Lopa lopa1238; cited by McGill & Blench 2012 as Blench n.d. b with file name 'West Kainji/Rop/Tsupamini wordlist '] -- annotated c. 400-item wordlist with sections on phonology (vowels, consonants, tones) and noun morphology; data collected by Blench with John Stark at Tsupamini, 26 Nov 1992.
new_statements.locator: sec. 1 Introduction p. 1 (p. 3); sec. 3.1 Vowels p. 2 (p. 4); sec. 3.3 Tones p. 3 (p. 5)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: quote-too-thin. Identity (Tsupamini list = Shuba/Cuba cbq) was independently verified by the checker against Blench & McGill 2012, and the remarks are Blench's own field notes, but 'tones are not marked.. will be added' and 'Tone on verb stems tends to be predictable' presuppose tone without stating an inventory or contrast; no stress remark. the PDF's metadata: 'Microsoft Word - Lopa wordlist paper.doc', Author Roger Blench, created 2 June 2006, 27 pp incl. front matter); the Internet Archive's index confirms captures of rogerblench.info '. Kainji/Lopa wordlist ' with status 200 on 20080723, 20090320 and 20101230 (the id_ URL A gives), 404 by 2024. All three quoted passage…
new_statements.relation_note: Only the three tone remarks quoted; phonology section otherwise gives an 8-vowel oral + 8-vowel nasal system, VV sequences, a consonant chart with labialisation/palatalisation, then noun-class prefix pairings. Wordlist itself is untoned except a handful of items (e.g. dàgá 'pot IV').
new_statements.rule_in_words: The language is treated as tonal: lexical items carry tones (left untranscribed in this preliminary list but audible on tape, with tonal changes across long vowels), and tone on verb stems is said to be largely predictable (implying lexically specified tone elsewhere, as in Kambari). No tone inventory is given and nothing at all is said about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the author calls the whole phonology 'based on rapid observations.. tentative' and the transcription 'very preliminary'
new_statements.identity_note: Catalogued everywhere as Lopa [lop]/lopa1238 because it predates the 2011-2014 recognition that 'Lopa' is two languages, but the data are from CUBA: p. 1 'collected.. from a group of villagers in Tsupamini on the 26th of November 1992'; Tsupamini = Cupamini = Cifamini (Hausa c = [tʃ]; ELAR 0145 records McGill's Tsucuba wordlist at 'Cupamini'; ISO CR 2014-036_cbq gives Cifamini 10°17'41"N 4°40'27"E as the Tsucuba centre; Blench & McGill 2012 sec. 3.2.3: Shuba major village ò̃tʃébá (Cifamini)). Decisive check: the 1992 forms are item-for-item the 'Shuba' column of Blench & McGill 2012 and exx. (6)-(7) 'Shuba' of Blench 2018 (nose ro-hɔ̃ro/a-hɔ̃ro, pot ruburu/a-ruburu, hair hĩ-bi/se-hĩ, salt ŋwá, ten obwa, eye ru-ɔmbi/a-ɔmbi, face a-haahũ, tongue ri-rimiya, neck rɔ-ɔɔru, arm taha, nail gungu, breast ri-hiŋga, urine səkãhã, beard bəibu/sə-bəibu, dog vavi, horse taaŋgo, work atomwarə -- every Shuba form checked is in this list), and Blench 2018 fn. 4 on Shuba ('when the data was collected, tones were not marked') matches this paper's p. 1. Blench's Atlas (2019 4th ed; 2020 ed. entry 445) accordingly lists the variety as 'Tsupamini', distinct from Rop. So this is a first-hand (if preliminary) source on cuba1236, not on Rop/lopa1238.

sources.note: Group-level only: northwest Kainji languages range 'from languages with extremely short lexemes with highly complex tonal systems to languages with long phonological words and restricted tone systems' (p. 92); Shen [=Laru] words 'more often monosyllabic with correspondingly more complex tonal inventories' (p. 105). Its reference list is what identifies Blench n.d. b ('The Lopa language of Northwestern Nigeria and its affinities') with the file 'West Kainji/Rop/Tsupamini wordlist ' -- the lead that re-identified works[0].
